This book is the first full textbook synthesis of multi-agent reinforcement learning, and its architecture is itself the first lesson. It builds a single ladder and then climbs it twice. The ladder is a hierarchy of interaction models: the normal-form game for one simultaneous encounter, the stochastic game that adds an evolving state driven by joint actions, and the partially observable stochastic game that adds private observations, with the single-agent MDP and POMDP recovered as special cases at one agent. On top of the models it places solution concepts, because in a multi-agent system the word optimal has no meaning until a solution concept supplies one: best response as the atomic operator, minimax for the two-agent zero-sum case, Nash equilibrium as mutual best response, then refinements and alternatives in Pareto optimality, social welfare and fairness, correlated equilibrium, and no-regret. Only after model and solution are fixed does the book talk about learning, and that ordering is a discipline the engine should copy: never ask how to learn before stating what game is being played and what would count as having solved it.
The computational substrate shared by everything is the single-agent machinery of Chapter 2. The Markov property licenses per-state values; the discounted return defines the objective; the Bellman equation turns value into a recursion, and the Bellman optimality equation turns the recursion into a fixed point whose greedy policy is optimal. think:
Halmos's Measure Theory is the book that turned a research specialty into a standard architecture, and reading it as an engineer means watching a complete measurement system get assembled from almost nothing. The raw materials are a space, classes of subsets of it, and the single demand that size should add over disjoint pieces. Everything else is forced by that demand plus one working decision: build on rings, classes closed under unions and differences, rather than on algebras or on all subsets. From rings the book gets generation (the smallest ring or sigma-ring over a class), the monotone class theorem as the practical tool for proving things about generated classes without constructing them, and a notion of measure as a countably additive, non negative set function. Countable additivity is the load-bearing axiom; the properties chapter shows it is equivalent, for finite additive set functions, to a single continuity condition, and the exercises carefully exhibit the counterexamples that show why no weaker hypothesis survives.

The second movement of the book is the extension machine, and it is the part with the most direct engineering content. A measure is usually easy to define on a small class (length on semiclosed intervals is the running example) and wanted on a large one. think: Start from the book's architecture, because the architecture is the argument. Barocas, Hardt, and Narayanan refuse to begin with metrics. They begin with the machine learning loop and with measurement: a target variable is chosen, data are collected under an existing social order, a model is fit, decisions are taken, and the decisions change the world that the next round of data describes. Only after legitimacy (should this system exist, and who says so) and after the philosophy of equality of opportunity do they allow the famous criteria onto the stage, and when the criteria arrive they arrive as three families of conditional independence statements about one joint distribution: independence of score and attribute, separation given the outcome, sufficiency given the score. The decisive move is to prove that these are not three dialects of one idea. With different base rates and imperfect prediction they are mutually incompatible, and the incompatibility is arithmetic, not political: the positive predictive value formula forces a choice. That single result reorganizes everything downstream. If no classifier can satisfy all criteria at once, then fairness work is not optimization but governance: someone must choose which criterion governs which surface, record the choice, and report the criteria being violated instead of hiding them. think: The second pass through the book reads it as a manual for evaluating any predictive system that ranks or scores people and things, which is the situation of a reasoning engine that publishes projections. The first operational lesson is the construct registry. Every predicted quantity in the book that goes wrong goes wrong at the target: cost for need, arrests for crime, test scores for performance. An engine that cannot state, for each output, what real quantity it stands for and what observable was actually used has not yet reached the starting line of the fairness discussion, or of the accuracy discussion either. The second lesson is that the score and the threshold are different artifacts with different owners. The threshold rule and the Bayes score belong to modeling; the threshold value belongs to policy, because it encodes the loss ratio and, under any fairness constraint, the chosen criterion. Keeping them separate is what makes the impossibility result manageable in practice: the model can stay excellent while the governance layer moves thresholds, applies post-processing, and records which criterion each move serves. The third lesson is calibration as semantics. A published number that audiences read as a probability incurs a debt: at every value, for every group, the realized frequency must match. think: This book builds all of finite-dimensional linear algebra from one refusal: nothing is allowed to be a matter of coordinates until the coordinate-free statement has been proved. The architecture is a chain of compressions. Chapter 1 fixes the arena, vector spaces and subspaces, and the idea of a sum of subspaces with unique representation. Chapter 2 adds counting: linear independence, span, bases, and then the length inequality, which is the quiet engine of the whole book, because it forces every basis to have the same length and thereby makes dimension a property of the space rather than of a chosen description. Chapter 3 studies maps between spaces. The fundamental theorem of linear maps, dim V equals dim null T plus dim range T, is a conservation law: a linear map cannot create dimension and cannot destroy it without recording the loss in its null space. Matrices enter only after that, as bookkeeping devices tied to bases, with the warning built into the theory that the matrix is not the map. Chapter 4 develops polynomials as an operator calculus in waiting, proving the division algorithm and the fundamental theorem of algebra, because the spectral theory of Chapter 5 needs roots. Eigenvalues are then defined without determinants, as the scalars where T minus lambda I stops being invertible, and the minimal polynomial appears as the smallest algebraic fingerprint of an operator: its zeros are the eigenvalues, its factor exponents measure Jordan coupling, and it divides eve

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Virtualization: transforming a physical resource into a virtual form of itself
quote: The primary way the OS does this is through a general technique that we call virtualization. That is, the OS takes a physical resource (such as the processor, or memory, or a disk) and transforms it into a more general, powerful, and easy-to-use virtual form of itself.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: The process: a running program summarized by its machine state
quote: The abstraction provided by the OS of a running program is something we will call a process. As we said above, a process is simply a running program; at any instant in time, we can summarize a process by taking an inventory of the different pieces of the system it accesses or affects during the course of its execution.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Separate policy from mechanism: how versus which
quote: You can think of the mechanism as providing the answer to a how question about a system; for example, how does an operating system perform a context switch? The policy provides the answer to a which question; for example, which process should the operating system run right now?

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Limited direct execution: run directly on the hardware, interpose only at key points
quote: To make a program run as fast as one might expect, not surprisingly OS developers came up with a technique, which we call limited direct execution.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: User mode and kernel mode: hardware-enforced privilege levels
quote: Thus, the approach we take is to introduce a new processor mode, known as user mode; code that runs in user mode is restricted in what it can do.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: The system call trap: simultaneous jump into the kernel and privilege raise
quote: To execute a system call, a program must execute a special trap instruction. This instruction simultaneously jumps into the kernel and raises the privilege level to kernel mode; once in the kernel, the system can now perform whatever privileged operations are needed (if allowed), and thus do the required work for the calling process.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: The timer interrupt: regaining control without cooperation
quote: A timer device can be programmed to raise an interrupt every so many milliseconds; when the interrupt is raised, the currently running process is halted, and a pre-configured interrupt handler in the OS runs. At this point, the OS has regained control of the CPU, and thus can do what it pleases: stop the current process, and start a different one.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: The context switch: save one process's registers, restore another's
quote: A context switch is conceptually simple: all the OS has to do is save a few register values for the currently-executing process (onto its kernel stack, for example) and restore a few for the soon-to-be-executing process (from its kernel stack).

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Turnaround time: completion minus arrival
quote: The turnaround time of a job is defined as the time at which the job completes minus the time at which the job arrived in the system.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: The convoy effect: short jobs queued behind a heavyweight consumer
quote: This problem is generally referred to as the convoy effect [B+79], where a number of relatively-short potential consumers of a resource get queued

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Response time: arrival to first scheduled run
quote: We define response time as the time from when the job arrives in a system to the first time it is scheduled

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Round robin: run a time slice, then switch to the next job in the run queue
quote: instead of running jobs to completion, RR runs a job for a time slice (sometimes called a scheduling quantum) and then switches to the next job in the run queue.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Multi-level feedback queue: priority learned from observed behavior
quote: Rather than giving a fixed priority to each job, MLFQ varies the priority of a job based on its observed behavior.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Lottery scheduling: tickets represent a process's share of a resource
quote: Underlying lottery scheduling is one very basic concept: tickets, which are used to represent the share of a resource that a process (or user or whatever) should receive.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: CFS virtual runtime: run the process with the lowest vruntime next
quote: As each process runs, it accumulates vruntime. In the most basic case, each process's vruntime increases at the same rate, in proportion with physical (real) time. When a scheduling decision occurs, CFS will pick the process with the lowest vruntime to run next.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: The address space: the running program's view of memory
quote: We call this abstraction the address space, and it is the running program's view of memory in the system.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Hardware address translation: every memory access is redirected
quote: Thus, on each and every memory reference, an address translation is performed by the hardware to redirect application memory references to their actual locations in memory.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Base and bounds (dynamic relocation): physical = virtual + base, checked against bounds
quote: Each memory reference generated by the process is a virtual address; the hardware in turn adds the contents of the base register to this address and the result is a physical address that can be issued to the memory system.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Segmentation: a base and bounds pair per logical segment
quote: instead of having just one base and bounds pair in our MMU, why not have a base and bounds pair per logical segment of the address space? A segment is just a contiguous portion of the address space of a particular length

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: External fragmentation: free space chopped into pieces too small to use
quote: the problem that exists is known as external fragmentation: the free space gets chopped into little pieces of different sizes and is thus fragmented; subsequent requests may fail because there is no single contiguous space that can satisfy the request, even though the total amount of free space exceeds the size of the request.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Paging: fixed-sized pages in the address space, page frames in physical memory
quote: Instead of splitting up a process's address space into some number of variable-sized logical segments (e.g., code, heap, stack), we divide it into fixed-sized units, each of which we call a page. Correspondingly, we view physical memory as an array of fixed-sized slots called page frames; each of these frames can contain a single virtual-memory page.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: The page table: per-process record of virtual-to-physical placement
quote: To record where each virtual page of the address space is placed in physical memory, the operating system usually keeps a per-process data structure known as a page table. The major role of the page table is to store address translations for each of the virtual pages of the address space, thus letting us know where in physical memory each page resides.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: The TLB: a hardware cache of popular address translations
quote: A TLB is part of the chip's memory-management unit (MMU), and is simply a hardware cache of popular virtual-to-physical address translations; thus, a better name would be an address-translation cache.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: AMAT: average memory access time from hit costs and miss probability
quote: Note you always pay the cost of accessing the data in memory; when you miss, however, you must additionally pay the cost of fetching the data from disk.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Optimal replacement (Belady MIN): evict the page used furthest in the future
quote: The optimal replacement policy leads to the fewest number of misses overall.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Race condition: results depend on the timing of execution
quote: What we have demonstrated here is called a race condition (or, more specifically, a data race): the results depend on the timing of the code's execution.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Critical section: code over shared state that must not run concurrently
quote: A critical section is a piece of code that accesses a shared variable (or more generally, a shared resource) and must not be concurrently executed by more than one thread.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Mutual exclusion: at most one thread inside the critical section
quote: What we really want for this code is what we call mutual exclusion. This property guarantees that if one thread is executing within the critical section, the others will be prevented from doing so.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Test-and-set: the atomic read-modify-write that builds a spin lock
quote: What the test-and-set instruction does is as follows. It returns the old value pointed to by the old_ptr, and simultaneously updates said value to new. The key, of course, is that this sequence of operations is performed atomically.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Mesa semantics: a signal is a hint, so always re-check the condition in a while loop
quote: Signaling a thread only wakes them up; it is thus a hint that the state of the world has changed (in this case, that a value has been placed in the buffer), but there is no guarantee that when the woken thread runs, the state will still be as desired.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Semaphore: an integer-valued object manipulated by wait and post
quote: we can see that sem_wait() will either return right away (because the value of the semaphore was one or higher when we called sem_wait()), or it will cause the caller to suspend execution waiting for a subsequent post.

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Deadlock: four necessary conditions, and prevention by breaking one
quote: Four conditions need to hold for a deadlock to occur

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Disk I/O time: seek plus rotation plus transfer
quote: we can now represent I/O time as the sum of three major components

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Journaling (write-ahead logging): write the note before overwriting in place
quote: By writing the note to disk, you are guaranteeing that if a crash takes places during the update (overwrite) of the structures you are updating, you can go back and look at the note you made and try again

title: dfc8529434c94df7
name: Wear leveling and write amplification in flash translation layers
quote: the FTL should try to spread writes across the blocks of the flash as evenly as possible, ensuring that all of the blocks of the device wear out at roughly the same time; doing so is called wear leveling

title: dfc8529434c94df7
think: Reading this book as an engine builder, the first thing to notice is that it is not really a book about operating systems features. It is a book about one repeated design situation: a shared physical substrate must be presented to many independent clients as if each owned it, under three simultaneous pressures, efficiency, control, and flexibility. Every chapter is that situation wearing different clothes. The CPU chapters solve it with limited direct execution: run the client code natively, because mediation on every instruction would be ruinously slow, and recover control only at traps and timer interrupts. The memory chapters solve it with address translation: interpose on every access, but do the interposition in hardware so it costs almost nothing, and let the OS program the translation state. The persistence chapters solve it with indirection again, page tables, translation layers, and journals, each time paying a small tax on the common path to buy safety on the rare path. That pattern, cheap common path plus checked rare path, is the deepest transferable idea in the book, and it should govern how our own platform treats model execution: native speed for the computation, interposition only at ingestion, emission, and resource boundaries. The second transferable idea is the mechanism and policy separation, stated in Chapter 4 and then honored for six hundred pages. Mechanisms in the book barely change once introduced: context switch, trap, translation, wait and signal.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Correctness splits into safety properties (nothing bad ever happens) and liveness properties (something good eventually happens)
quote: Safety properties, of the form “nothing bad ever happens” or, more precisely, “there are no bad reachable configurations.”

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Liveness is a property of whole executions with a finite witness time, not of single states
quote: These are not properties of particular states (I might unhappily await the eventual delivery of my email for decades without violating the liveness property just described), but of executions, where the property must hold starting at some finite time.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Asynchronous model: messages are delivered eventually after unknown delay, with no timing bound
quote: Such systems are difficult to build when the components become too numerous or too widely dispersed, but they are often easier to analyze than asynchronous systems, where messages are only delivered eventually after some unknown delay.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Time complexity of a terminating protocol is the time of the last event at any process
quote: The time complexity of a protocol (that terminates) is the time of the last event at any process.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Message complexity of a terminating protocol is the total number of messages sent
quote: For a protocol that terminates, the message complexity is the total number of messages sent.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Flooding: forward a message to all neighbors unless it has been seen before, tracked with one seen bit
quote: The idea is that when a process receives a message M , it forwards it to all of its neighbors unless it has seen it before, which it tracks using a single bit seen-message.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Flooding reaches every process within diameter time D and at most one message per edge
quote: Theorem 3.1.1. Every process receives M after at most D time and at most |E| messages, where D is the diameter of the network and E is the set of (directed) edges in the network.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Convergecast inverts broadcast: data flows from all nodes up a spanning tree to the root under a summary function
quote: A convergecast is the inverse of broadcast: instead of a message propagating down from a single root to all nodes, data is collected from outlying nodes to the root.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: A synchronizer transforms synchronous protocols into asynchronous protocols at small complexity cost
quote: Sometimes this can be dealt with by applying a synchronizer (Chapter 7), which transforms synchronous protocols into asynchronous protocols at a small cost in complexity.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Angluin barrier: leader election in a ring is impossible without distinct starting identities
quote: A classic result of Angluin [Ang80] shows that leader election in a ring is impossible if the processes do not start with distinct identities.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Causal shuffles, permutations consistent with happens before, are exactly the schedules indistinguishable from the original
quote: A causal shuffle S 0 of a schedule S is a permutation of S that is consistent with the happens-before relation on S; that is, if e happens-before e0 in S, then e precedes e0 in S 0 .

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Lamport clock: increment on local events, piggyback on messages, and on receipt set clock to max of local and received plus one
quote: Lamport’s logical clock [Lam78] runs on top of any other message-passing protocol, adding additional state at each process and additional content to the messages (which is invisible to the underlying protocol).

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Chandy Lamport snapshot: initiator broadcasts a snap marker, each process records state on first receipt and forwards the marker
quote: Here some central initiator broadcasts a snap message, and each process records its state and immediately forwards the snap message to all neighbors when it first receives a snap message.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Coordinated attack: with lossy channels no protocol guarantees agreement unless the outcome is predetermined
quote: The interesting property of the problem is that if carrier pigeons can become lost, there is no protocol that guarantees agreement in all cases unless the outcome is predetermined (e.g., the generals always attack no matter what happens).

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Synchronous agreement by flooding sets for f plus 1 rounds, then decide by a fixed function of the common set
quote: At round f + 1, I decide on f (S), where f is some fixed function from sets of process-input pairs to outputs that picks some input in S: for example, f might take the input with the smallest process-id attached to it, take the max of all known input values, or take the majority of all known input values.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Exponential information gathering: state is a tree of who heard what from whom, decided after f plus 1 rounds
quote: The idea of exponential information gathering is that each process will do a lot of gossiping, but now its state is no longer just a flat set of inputs, but a tree describing who it heard what from.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Phase king: run f plus 1 voted phases, each coordinated by a preselected king, so at least one phase has an honest king
quote: The main idea of the algorithm is that we avoid the recursive majority voting of EIG by running a vote in each of f + 1 phases through a phase king, some process chosen in advance to run the phase.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: FLP impossibility: no agreement protocol in an asynchronous message passing system tolerates even one crash failure
quote: The Fischer-Lynch-Paterson (FLP) result [FLP85] says something much stronger: you can’t do agreement in an asynchronous message-passing system if even one crash failure is allowed.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Bivalence method: a configuration is bivalent when executions from it can still decide either value, and impossibility keeps the system bivalent forever
quote: A configuration that is not bivalent is univalent, or more specifically 0-valent or 1-valent depending on whether all executions starting in the configuration produce 0 or 1 as the decision value.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Paxos two phase voting: prepare extracts a promise and the highest accepted proposal, then accept with majority wins
quote: An accepter responds to this with a promise never to accept any proposal with a number less than r (so that old proposals don’t suddenly get ratified) together with the highest-numbered proposal that the accepter has accepted (so that the proposer can substitute this value for its own, in case the previous value was in fact ratified).

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Multi Paxos: repeated one shot Paxos instances implement a replicated state machine log
quote: The version that is more typically used, called multi-Paxos, uses repeated executions of the basic Paxos algorithm to implement a replicated state machine; we’ll describe this in §12.7.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Failure detector taxonomy: suspicion of faulty processes is graded as completeness, suspicion of correct processes as accuracy
quote: Suspicion of faulty processes comes under the heading of completeness; of non-faulty processes, accuracy.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Quorum system: a family of subsets of processes with pairwise intersection, turning coordination into combinatorics
quote: This is a special case of a quorum system, a family of subsets of the set of processes with the property that any two subsets in the family overlap.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Sybil attack: one faulty participant overwhelms minority fault assumptions with an army of virtual clones
quote: But this possibility allows for a Sybil attack [Dou02], where an algorithm naively implemented on the assumption that faulty processes form a small minority is suddenly overwhelmed by a single faulty machine backed by an army of virtual clones.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Attiya Bar Noy Dolev register: writes and reads complete after majority acknowledgment with timestamps picking the newest value
quote: To write a value, the writer increments its timestamp, updates its value and sends write(value, timestamp) to all other processes.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Linearizability: every concurrent execution has a sequential linearization respecting real time order of non overlapping operations
quote: The strongest consistency property generally used is linearizability [HW90], which says roughly that an implementation of an object is linearizable if, for any complete concurrent execution of the object, there is a sequential execution of the object with the same operations and return values, where the (total) order of operations in the sequential execution is a linearization of the (partial) order of operations in the concurrent execution.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Read modify write registers apply a function to state and write it back as one atomic action, including test and set, fetch and add, and compare and swap
quote: These usually go by the name of read-modify-write (RMW) registers, since the additional operations consist of reading the state, applying some function to it, and writing the state back, all as a single atomic action.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Mutual exclusion primitives exist so at most one process at a time works on a shared data structure
quote: These are all designed to solve various forms of mutual exclusion or locking, where we want at most one process at a time to work on some shared data structure.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Splitter: arriving processes are diverted right, down, or stop, giving a solo process a fast path into mutual exclusion
quote: A splitter assigns to each processes that arrives at it the value right, down, or stop.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Wait free hierarchy: object types are classified by consensus number, the largest n for which they solve wait free consensus
quote: The wait-free hierarchy hrm classifies asynchronous shared-memory object types T by consensus number, where a type T has consensus number n if with objects of type T and atomic registers (all initialized to appropriate values1 ) it is possible to solve wait-free consensus (i.e., agreement, validity, wait-free termination) for n processes but not for n + 1 processes.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Atomic snapshot by double collect: if two successive collects agree exactly, no write intervened and the vector is a valid snapshot
quote: We can now detect if a new write has occurred between two reads of the same variable.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Renaming: processes starting with names from a huge namespace must acquire unique names from a much smaller namespace
quote: In the renaming problem, we have n processes, each starts with a name from some huge namespace, and we’d like to assign them each unique names from a much smaller namespace.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Self stabilization: from any arbitrary starting configuration the system eventually reaches a legal configuration and stays there
quote: A self-stabilizing algorithm has the property that, starting from any arbitrary configuration, it eventually reaches a legal configuration, and this property is stable in the sense that it remains in a legal configuration thereafter.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Population protocols compute by pairwise interactions of finite state agents under global fairness, converging to the output without termination detection
quote: Computation by population protocols usually consists of computing some function of the initial states of the population and propagating the output of this function to all agents.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
name: Approximate agreement relaxes consensus to outputs within epsilon of each other and inside the input range, and is wait free solvable
quote: Validity Every process returns an output within the range of inputs.

title: ebb8bb7e264a9641
think: This book is a complete theory of what can and cannot be computed when many processes must act together without a shared clock, a shared memory they can trust, or reliable communication, and its value for a reasoning engine is that it supplies the coordination physics underneath every multi source, multi module system. The architecture of the notes moves in three great arcs. The first arc is message passing. It begins by fixing the model with unusual care: processes, channels, executions, safety and liveness, and the two complexity currencies of time and messages. On that foundation it builds the elementary circulation patterns, flooding for broadcast and convergecast for aggregation, then breadth first search, then leader election, where Angluin symmetry barrier already teaches that identical agents with identical inputs cannot break symmetry without identities or randomness. Causal ordering and logical clocks follow, because once messages can be delayed arbitrarily the system needs its own notion of time: happens before, Lamport clocks that extend causality cheaply, vector clocks that capture it exactly at linear cost, and consistent snapshots that define what a global state can even mean when no two processes observe simultaneously. Synchronizers then show how to import synchronous designs into asynchronous reality, and immediately the limits appear: coordinated attack shows common knowledge is unattainable over lossy channels, synchronous agreement works by flooding for f
